processor: IonQ diamond-core quantum memory (modular networking component)
notes: Announced 2026-04-14. IonQ selected for DARPA's Heterogeneous Architectures for Quantum (HARQ) program. HARQ aims to build networked quantum computers combining distinct qubit types (trapped ions, neutral atoms, superconducting) into high-performance modular architectures. IonQ's role: quantum memories fabricated from quantum-grade synthetic diamond, designed for datacenter-scale interconnects and long-distance entanglement distribution. HARQ is a platform-agnostic networking program — NOT a single-vendor hardware initiative. This is a government validation of IonQ's modular networking roadmap, not a new QPU specification. RELEVANCE TO OUR WORK: Low direct relevance for near-term MERA experiments. Strategically important: if HARQ succeeds, it creates heterogeneous quantum computing infrastructure (trapped-ion + neutral atom hybrid) that would be ideal for fault-tolerant holographic MERA circuits combining the high-fidelity gate operations of trapped ions with the large qubit counts of neutral atoms. Timeline: HARQ is a multi-year DARPA program; deployable results expected 2028-2030.
